messages:
security-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Unusual KMS decrypt spike detected for key 'projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/model-serving'. 3.8x baseline in last 12m. Investigate.
mia chen: seeing the alert now, pulling logs. tagging infra for possible burst. :eyes:
raj patel: grabbing Cloud Audit Logs -- looks like a series of decrypts from a single service account service-account@redwood-prod.ipsvc. Started 2026-03-02T12:05Z.
raj patel: snippet:```
2026-03-02T12:06:08Z decrypt key=model-serving svc_acc=svc-model-batch region=us-west1
2026-03-02T12:07:02Z decrypt key=model-serving svc_acc=svc-model-batch region=us-west1
2026-03-02T12:07:59Z decrypt key=model-serving svc_acc=svc-model-batch region=us-west1
```
mia chen: any unusual deploys around 12:00?
olivia ng: no scheduled deploys in that window. CI doesn't show a batch job either. Could be a runaway job or compromised creds.
tomas berg: if it's a runaway job, RBAC should limit scope. Do we have recent policy changes on that service account?
raj patel: checked IAM change history — no policy edits in last 7 days. However, the service account key was rotated 3 weeks ago. No suspicious console logins.
olivia ng: containment suggestion: temporarily revoke decrypt permission from svc-model-batch, create a new key version for model-serving, and force rotation for any callers.
mia chen: agree. Plan: (1) revoke roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on svc-model-batch, (2) create new key version and set primary to v2, (3) update deployment envs to use new key version or use KMS alias, (4) export audit logs to secure bucket for forensics. Doing step 1 now.
security-bot: Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kms-anomaly - contains checklist for revocation and log export.
raj patel: revocation applied. Confirmed 403s for new decrypt attempts from that service account. :white_check_mark:
mia chen: creating new key version v2 and promoting it. tagging sec oncall for visibility.
tomas berg: after we promote v2, we should rotate client credentials on any services that legitimately need access. Also propose a short-lived allowlist policy for known egress IPs.
olivia ng: starting log export to gs://redwood-sec-logs/kms-spike/1769501120/ with object ACLs locked down. ETA ~4m.
raj patel: forensic note: observed ~420 decrypt ops between 12:05-12:17. Origin ASN looks like cloud provider internal (us-west1 compute). We'll correlate instance ids next.
emma cruz: drafting internal advisory for execs. Draft: "We detected and contained anomalous KMS decrypt activity affecting a model-serving key. We revoked the implicated service account and promoted a new key version. No evidence of data exfiltration so far. Investigation ongoing; we will update within 3 hours." Thoughts?
mia chen: short + clear. add that customer-facing keys and customer data were not involved (if true).
emma cruz: added sentence: "Customer-managed keys and tenant data not implicated; this affects infra encryption keys only." OK?
tomas berg: approve. Also add next steps: audit log export, RBAC review, and postmortem with mitigation timeline.
raj patel: correlation complete: decrypts originated from a batch-node pool instance group; instance identity indicates a leaked short-lived token from a CI job that was misconfigured to use prod SA.
mia chen: root cause hypothesis: CI job used prod SA due to variable misconfig in pipeline. No lateral movement detected.
olivia ng: action items: (A) CI pipeline variable fix and rotate any tokens, (B) restrict SA usage via workload identity where possible, (C) add a detection rule for sudden decrypt rate spikes, (D) schedule RBAC audit of all prod SAs.
emma cruz: customer comm draft (short): "We identified and contained unusual internal key activity impacting infrastructure encryption keys. There is no sign of customer data access or exfiltration. We have applied mitigations and are conducting a full review; we will notify customers if we find evidence of impact"
security-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0032 and paged sec-oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0032
mia chen: putting a quick exec update in #exec-updates: "Containment complete; new key version promoted; revocation applied; investigation ongoing; no customer impact identified."
raj patel: exporting full audit log bundle and checksums to forensics bucket. Also snapshotting disk images of implicated instances per forensics SOP.
tomas berg: post-incident items: 1) enforce workload identity for CI jobs, 2) short TTL for any remaining service account keys, 3) automated anomaly alert tuning, 4) mini security training for infra/ci owners. Assigning owners after postmortem.
mia chen: timeline notes for postmortem: detection 12:05Z, revocation 12:18Z, key promotion 12:22Z, export started 12:23Z.
emma cruz: thanks team. I'll finalize customer and exec drafts once we confirm no customer access. Please add any facts you want included.
raj patel: will add instance ids and the CI job name to the incident ticket in 15m.
mia chen: closing this thread for now — moving ongoing updates to the INC ticket. If anything new pops up, call sec-oncall immediately. :lock:"
